title: TGFBIp expression adds prognostic information in an ovarian-cancer ML study
summary: In a retrospective tissue-microarray cohort of 155 epithelial ovarian-cancer patients, support vector machine and random forest models combined clinicopathological features with tumor and stromal TGFBIp expression. Adding both expression compartments improved held-out vital-status discrimination by a reported AUC difference of 0.038 (95% CI 0.002–0.092). Validation was internal, follow-up duration varied, and binary endpoints did not model event timing or censoring. Recurrence specificity and calibration were limited, and clinical utility remains unproven.

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: Internal held-out prediction and paired-bootstrap incremental-value comparison.
evidence.unknown: External validation, time-to-event performance, treatment confounding and clinical benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Twelve algorithms compared across four expression-inclusion strategies; preprocessing/tuning/model selection limited to training data, 155-patient retrospective cohort and held-out final evaluation. Specific biomarker incremental-value result, not a clinical-benefit claim.
